procedures.title: Four-speed transmissions (Muncie and Saginaw): general description
notes: Muncie 4-speed: synchromesh, helical gears throughout, built for high torque without extra weight and for high speed without excess heat or friction loss; parts held to close tolerances for long heavy use.

Muncie main drive gear rides on a heavy-duty ball bearing at the front of the case and pilots in an oil-impregnated bushing in the crankshaft. The mainshaft front pilots in rollers inside the main drive gear; its rear rides on a heavy-duty ball bearing in a retainer at the rear of the case.
Muncie countergear runs on double rows of rollers at each end with thrust washers against the case bosses. The two-piece reverse idler runs on bronze bushings with thrust washers front and rear.
